about: Published local-inference benchmarks (mostly llama-bench pp/tg), every number copied from the cited source. tools/fit-families.mjs fits the per-family factors on the rows the model can represent; tools/accuracy.mjs reports estimate vs published for each.

fields.pp: {tokens, tps}: prompt processing, e.g. pp512 is tokens 512
fields.fileGB: the size as printed, in fileUnit (llama-bench prints GiB)
fields.flashAttention: 0/1/null (null: not stated or the default of that build)
fields.date: the llama.cpp commit date for scoreboard rows (the run may be later), else the post date

caveats: Build drift: the same hardware gains up to +33% tg and 2-4x pp across llama.cpp builds (M2 Ultra 2023-2026, Strix Halo ROCm, DGX Spark launch week vs Feb 2026).
Flash attention raises pp on CUDA and Strix Halo and lowers it on Intel; compare rows with the same setting.
Same label, different bytes: gpt-oss "Q4_K_M" keeps MXFP4 experts; early builds labelled the MXFP4 file BF16 at 12.83 GiB; unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL is not Q4_K_M. Use fileGB, not the label.
Test shapes differ: pp512 vs pp2048 with -ub 2048; tg128 vs tg32/tg16; batched-bench tg is an aggregate over the streams.
Build options: SYCL fp16 builds give about 3x the pp of fp32 builds with the same tg; a MinGW build decoded 5.4x slower than MSVC.
Scoreboards keep the highest submission per device, which biases them up.

One bandwidth fraction per family does not fit datacenter GPUs: a 3.8 GB model reaches 60-80% of nominal bandwidth on consumer GPUs and Apple, about 17% on the MI300X, so a fixed per-token overhead is needed.
